behavioral_notes.observation: utm.mixin is an AbstractModel inherited by downstream records (crm.lead, mailing.mailing, link.tracker, etc.). On any web request ir.http._post_dispatch -> _set_utm reads the utm_campaign/utm_source/utm_medium GET params and writes them into long-lived (31-day) optional cookies (odoo_utm_campaign/source/medium) keyed on the request host. When a record that inherits utm.mixin is created, default_get iterates tracking_fields() and back-fills campaign_id/source_id/medium_id from those cookies, resolving string values to records via _find_or_create_record. UTM defaulting is deliberately skipped for internal salespeople (group_sale_salesman) unless run as superuser. This attribution wiring is invisible to metadata.

find_or_create_record is the frontend-facing wrapper (used in website_links) returning {'id','name'} rather than a recordset because call_kw's create magic is bypassed. For models in _tracking_models() (the utm.* comodels of the tracking fields) it delegates to _find_or_create_record, which does a case-insensitive ('name','=ilike') search with active_test=False and creates the record only if missing, flagging is_auto_campaign=True for utm.campaign. Non-UTM inherited models fall through to a plain create on _rec_name, so the helper stays ACL-safe.

utm.campaign, utm.source and utm.medium each carry a SQL UNIQUE(name) constraint and route create() through utm.mixin._get_unique_names, which appends a bracketed counter ('test' -> 'test [2]') so duplicate/concurrent inserts never collide. utm.campaign also computes its name from the translatable title via _get_unique_names with utm_check_skip_record_ids=self.ids so a record never bumps its own counter. The dedup/counter logic (regex _split_name_and_count + Domain.OR search_read) lives entirely in Python and is invisible to schema metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: utm.campaign Kanban stages + utm.source.mixin name generation + delete guards
behavioral_notes.observation: utm.campaign uses utm.stage (Many2one, ondelete='restrict', default=first stage) with _group_expand_stage_ids so the Kanban renders every pipeline stage even when empty - stages are the campaign workflow columns. utm.source.mixin is the consumer pattern (mailing/social post): create() auto-creates a utm.source per record and derives its name from the host record's _rec_name content via utm.source._generate_name, keeping source naming consistent across downstream models. utm.medium guards six load-bearing reference mediums (Email/Direct/Website/X/Facebook/LinkedIn) and utm.source guards the 'Referral' source against deletion via @api.ondelete.

1 JS file (utm_campaign_kanban_examples.js), 0 XML templates, 0 OWL components, 1 registry registration (kanban_examples:utm_campaign), 0 patches; single asset bundle ['web.assets_backend']. The JS only seeds Kanban 'examples' (starter stage layouts) for the campaign board; no client components or services.

information_flows: side-effect: ir.http._post_dispatch -> _set_utm writes utm_* GET params into odoo_utm_* cookies (31-day, host-scoped)
side-effect: utm.mixin.default_get reads odoo_utm_* cookies -> back-fills campaign_id/source_id/medium_id on inheriting records (crm.lead, mailing.mailing, link.tracker)
side-effect: create() on campaign/source/medium -> utm.mixin._get_unique_names dedups names with a bracketed counter

capabilities: Attribute Records via Tracking Cookies & URL Parameters
value_streams: Attribution back-fill: web visit (utm_* params) -> tracking cookies -> campaign/source/medium stamped on the created record (lead/mailing/link)
policies: SQL UNIQUE(name) on campaign/source/medium enforced via _get_unique_names counter
ondelete guards: protected reference mediums (Email/Direct/Website/X/Facebook/LinkedIn) and the 'Referral' source cannot be deleted
UTM defaulting skipped for internal salespeople (group_sale_salesman) unless superuser
stakeholders: Downstream marketing/sales modules (mass_mailing, crm, sale, link_tracker, social)
metrics: Aggregate stats surfaced by consumers (e.g. mailing/click counts added onto utm.campaign downstream)

classification.apqc_category: 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services
classification.rationale: utm is cross-cutting marketing-attribution mixin and reference data (campaign/source/medium/tag/stage) consumed by many primary marketing/sales modules (mass_mailing, crm, sale, link_tracker, social); it is foundational, not a value stream of its own. It owns no operational document chain and exposes no value-creating service - its contribution is campaign attribution and marketing administration (APQC 3.0, marketing performance/admin), so it is a support activity rather than a chain/shop/network primary.

standard_capabilities: campaign / source / medium / tag reference data with enforced unique names
utm.mixin trait that stamps campaign/source/medium on any inheriting record
cookie + URL-param attribution wired through ir.http dispatch
campaign Kanban with configurable stages and starter examples
auto find-or-create of UTM records from free text (find_or_create_record)
typical_fits: attributing leads, mailings and tracked links to a campaign/source/medium
standard last-touch web attribution via utm_* query parameters
organizing campaigns into pipeline stages with tags and a responsible user
common_gaps: no multi-touch / weighted attribution model (last cookie wins)
no campaign budget, spend or ROI tracking out of the box
no analytics views of its own (pivot/graph 0) - reporting comes from consumers
no portal/public UI; backend-only reference administration

open_questions: Exact set of downstream models that inherit utm.mixin / utm.source.mixin and how each overrides tracking_fields (resolvable only when consumer modules are installed).
Whether consumers (mass_mailing, link_tracker, social) add A/B-test and click/mailing-count aggregates onto utm.campaign at runtime.
Live row counts / real campaign data were not captured (runtime models_with_data=0).
